To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology of the catalyst plays a significant role in the electrochemical oxidation of ethanol.

the Pd(100)-faceted nanobars supported on carbon black (NB/C) showed the highest catalytic electroactivity with respect to ethanol oxidation, followed by the Pd(111)-faceted nanoparticles (NP/C), Pd(110)-faceted nanorods (NB/C) supported on carbon black, and commercial Pd/C.
the Pd nanobars catalyst presented the highest electroactivity with respect to the ethanol electro-oxidization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of Pd catalysts with different structures and their application as catalysts for ethanol electro-oxidations.
the development of a new Pd-based catalyst with a high activity for ethanol oxidation in alkaline media, which is a key step for the direct alcohol fuel cell (DAFC) development.
the effect of the crystal structure of the Pd nanoparticles on the ethanol electro-oxidative activity in alkaline media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pd(100)-based electrocatalysts are more efficient in ethanol oxidation than Pd(111) or Pd(110) based electrocatalysts.
the Pd catalysts with different crystallographic structures have different catalytic activities for the electro-oxidation of ethanol, which was confirmed by cyclic voltammetry.
, in terms of ethanol electro-oxidative reaction, the catalyst with the highest activity was the Pd nanobars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pd(100)-based catalysts are the most active for the oxidation of ethanol.
the electro-oxidation of ethanol is more active on a Pd catalyst with a high percentage of Pd(100).

the Pd catalyst with the most exposed Pd(100), Pd(100)/Pd(111), Pd(111)/Pd(100) and Pd(100)/(111) facets, which is the nanobars (Pd NB), showed the best catalytic activity towards the electro-oxidation of ethanol in acidic media, followed by the Pd NP, Pd NR and commercial Pd/C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of ethanol oxidation, Pd nanobars are more active than nanoparticles, nanorods or commercial Pd/C.
the Pd(100)-rich catalysts are more active for ethanol oxidation than Pd(111)-rich ones.
the catalytic activity of the electrocatalysts can be modulated by controlling the crystallographic structure of the Pd nanoparticles.
